trial_court: II Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Bengaluru, MC No.531/2013 and MC No.1964/2011
case_name: J. Chandra Prakash vs V. B. Sujatha @ Pooja
facts_of_case: The parties are J. Chandra Prakash and V.B. Sujatha @ Pooja. The husband filed a petition under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, which was dismissed by the trial court. The wife filed a petition under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, which was allowed by the trial court.

legal_principles.principle: Parties can settle disputes amicably and withdraw cases.
legal_principles.held: Our attention has been invited to the memo which has been duly signed by the appellant as well as respondent.

legal_principles.principle: Permanent alimony can be settled through a compromise.
legal_principles.held: In terms of the settlement arrived at between the parties, the appellants-husband is required to pay a sum of Rs.12,00,000/- to the respondent-wife herein, in full and final settlement of the claim of the respondent-wife as permanent alimony.

outcome.final_order: The appeals were allowed and the judgment and decree passed by the trial court were set aside.

use_for_drafting: drafting divorce petition under Hindu Marriage Act
appealing family court judgment to High Court
seeking divorce on grounds of irretrievable breakdown
